show.name: A Child's Christmas
show.description:
By Dylan Thomas and Richard Burton.

A Child's Christmas in Wales by Dylan Thomas ‘Snow grew overnight on the roofs of the houses’ 

Dylan Thomas and Richard Burton are icons of twentieth century Wales. They have produced stories about Christmases in Wales that rival Charles Dickens’ short stories about Christmas in nineteenth century England. In some ways Thomas and Burton can be accused of inventing Christmas in exactly the same way Dickens is responsible for creating the Christmas that we enjoy so wholeheartedly. 

For all of that, however, Burton and Thomas were actors whose love of words shines through these two short but heart-warming stories. 

Described by the South Wales Evening Post as ‘a joy’, this ‘Welsh Icons Xmas show’ performed by two actors has proved hugely popular - Join Lighthouse as they conjure up Christmas in the air.... "

 Mae'r Nadolig wedi ddechre'n bendant nawr." 
"Two mesmerising performances. A wonderful afternoon of festive theatre." 

‘There were very few white Christmases in my part of Wales’…. 
A Christmas Story by Richard Burton

show.name: Amelia Coburn
show.description:
Amelia Coburn has a knack for making the unusual sound timeless. 
Her honest, occasionally hilarious and quintessentially north-eastern persona disarms and beguiles in equal measure. 
Drawing inspiration from gothic literature and the shadowy allure of film noir, there is a darkness at the heart of many of her songs, populated by vivid characters and nocturnal creatures that inhabit the liminal space “between the moon and the milkman”. 

Amelia has supported  the likes of The Levellers, Rianne Downey, Hamish Hawk, Stornoway, Rumer and Katherine Priddy.
Amelia had her own sold-out Royal Albert Hall ‘Elgar Room’ show and mesmerising performances at some of the UK’s best loved boutique festivals. 
A sold-out solo headline UK tour in early 2026 solidified her burgeoning reputation, with slots alongside Paul Weller, Suzanne Vega and The Proclaimers showcasing Amelia’s sound to ever increasing audiences. 

With a new album around the corner, Amelia embarks on her biggest full band headline show!

"A great voice with great tunes" - Paul Weller in Mojo Magazine 
"In a cynical, meta-obsessed world, her music is wide-eyed, guileless and fresh" - The Arts Desk (Album of the Year) 
“A world full of darkness and light and soundtracked by magic and melancholy” - Louder Than War
  “Songs that feel like centuries old fairy tales” - Shindig! Magazine 
 “What a voice! Really, really lovely” - Jo Whiley, BBC Radio 2

Amelia will be supported by the fabulous Domino Lewis

Domino Lewis is singer-songwriter based in Paris, France. 
These past couple years, Domino played on stage in the States, touring in Austin, Nashville, Knoxville, Roanoke and D.C, as well as a short European tour across Switzerland and Germany. 
She opened for Texas guitarist Hayden Pedigo and country star Esther Rose in Paris, for Niamh Regan in London, Kelsey Waldon in Cologne, played at the historic Francofolies festival, Kerwax and bluegrass Herbe Bleue festival, as well as the famous Hyperweekend Festival (Radio France’s very own event).

Tickets £16.50

show.name: Danny Hart’s Won’t Sit Down
show.description:
Danny Hart isn’t just part of downhill mountain biking’s elite — he defines it. A two‑time World Champion, Red Bull Hardline conqueror, multiple National Champion and double World Cup overall silver medallist, the legendary Redcar Rocket has carved his name into the sport’s history with raw speed, fearless commitment and one of the most iconic World Championship runs ever witnessed. 

In Won’t Sit Down, Danny brings his trademark dry wit and ice‑cool composure to the stage, guiding audiences through the adrenaline, the chaos and the triumphs of a life lived at full throttle. From the early days on the bike to the pressure cooker of racing at the highest level, he lifts the curtain on what it really takes to become a World Champion — the grit, the grind, the glory, and everything in between.   This is your chance to experience the stories, the mindset and the moments that shaped one of mountain biking’s true greats. Strap in — Danny Hart is ready to take you for a ride.

show.name: Pride and Prejud(ish)
show.description:
Black RAT Productions and Blackwood Miners’ Institute present A new comedy by Richard Tunley

Starring ZOË DAVIES, JEMIMA NICHOLAS, OLIVIA EDWARDS & KATE POWELL 

Hot on the heels of Dai Cula: Prince of the Valleys, Black RAT Productions returns with a riotous new comedy where Jane Austen collides headfirst with modern South Wales. 

Austen-and-Bridgerton obsessive Lizzie Bennet dreams of classier times - but keeping hold of that fantasy is difficult when her family is on the brink of collapse. 
While Mam is living her best life in Spain, Lizzie is left holding the fort as her sisters unravel around her. 
Lydia has turned full Bridezilla over the wedding of the century, Jane is struggling with her own fragile marriage, Kitty is threatening to boycott the big day, and Mary? Mary went to Uni… and hasn’t been back since. 
As the wedding day hurtles closer, tensions rise, secrets spill, and family pride collides with very modern prejudices. Performed in Black RAT’s signature high-energy style, this physical comedy is brilliantly bonkers! 
Recommended for ages 14+ 
Supported by Arts Council of Wales

show.description:
Lighthouse Theatre and Pontardawe Arts Centre present WAFR: 
Playhouse of the Air in 
The Chimes: Dickens on Air 
'A Festive Story to Ring the Old Year Out and the New Year In.' 

 It is Christmas 1950 in New York and the actors of WAFR: Playhouse of the Air gather for their annual festive broadcast...There is a new government, a new hope, a new world, so what bet-ter than a new play? And there is no better story-teller than Charles Dickens - and there is no better man to keep Christmas than he! 

 Trotty Veck is a ticket-porter – a man who fetches and carries packages, letters and deliveries for a small sixpence here and there. He doesn’t have much but he is happy, gentle and lives a simple, obedient life. That life is given its order by the sound of the bells of his local church – breakfast, lunch, dinner all from the sound of the bells. He sometimes even hears them speaking to him… In the run-up to the festive season Trotty falls asleep after a long day’s carrying and delivering. Woken by the church bells, The Chimes, and then summoned up the tower by their mysterious power, he has just one chance to change this world… but will he listen to the bells? The Chimes is a Victorian It’s a Wonderful Life filled with all of the master story-teller’s colourful characters and heart-rending poignancy. 

Fresh from their hugely popular adaptations of A Christmas Carol and Casablanca, Lighthouse Theatre brings their signature live radio play style to this classic by the most theatrical of authors. There will be jingles, carols, music and – of course – bells!…this show is sure to be fast and funny, inventive and entertaining; but most of all a Christmas treat to reinforce the message of this festive time of the year… 

Recommended for ages 10 and above. 
Presented in conjunction with Arts Council Wales

show.name: The Ghost Light- with Owen Staton
show.description:
When every audience has gone home, one light remains burning on the stage. 
The Ghost Light............. 
For generations it has stood watch in empty theatres, gathering stories in the silence until someone is ready to tell them. 

This October, join me, Owen Staton, host of the Time Between Times Storytelling podcast, for The Ghost Light—an evening of live storytelling in one of the most atmospheric places imaginable: Pontardawe Arts Centre. 
Over the course of the evening I'll share a collection of haunting tales rooted in the place we're gathered. Every performance is unique, drawing on local ghost stories, forgotten folklore and strange true accounts from the surrounding area. From lonely roads and abandoned houses to ancient churches, quiet woodlands and restless spirits that refuse to leave the places they once called home, these are the stories that have shaped the landscape around us for generations. 

A storyteller. An audience. A theatre wrapped in darkness, save for the ghost light burning on the stage.
 
As the evening unfolds, you'll laugh, you'll wonder and, perhaps, you'll find yourself looking a little more carefully into the shadows as you leave. The stories will carry you through encounters with uncanny visitors, ancient curses, mysterious disappearances, spectral figures and moments when the ordinary world gives way to something altogether stranger. 
Each tale is told in the rich oral tradition that has made Time Between Times Storytelling one of Britain's most-loved folklore podcasts. These are stories shaped not by special effects but by voice, imagination and the shared experience of sitting together exactly as our ancestors have done for centuries. 
No two performances are the same, because every town has its own ghosts. 
Every theatre has its own silence. 
And every audience brings something different to the telling. 
When the house lights fade and the ghost light begins to glow, take your seat and listen carefully. The stories are here 

 “Owen is one of the finest storytellers I know. His tales are crafted with ingenuity and warmth, bringing to life stories ancient and new. … A rare gift indeed.” — Nat Doig, Podcast Host (Weird in the Wade) 

“If you’re looking for some incredible tales told by a master storyteller, check out his podcast Time Between Times. You will not be disappointed.” — Shannon Bailey Grace, Storyteller & Podcast Host (Ghost and Grub) 

“Bingeworthy and spooky traditional tales. Time Between Times Storytelling with Owen Staton brings Welsh folk-history to life.” — Gregg Stockdale, The Podcast Geek

show.name: The Silent Volunteer
show.description:
In a moving tribute to all those affected by the Aberfan disaster, The Silent Volunteer asks the question, “Have we learnt from our mistakes?” Lovingly performed by a cast affected by what happened that Friday morning 60 years ago, the play explores the enormous role volunteers played in the aftermath, and how the events of 1966 have continued to shape mining communities ever since. 

The Silent Volunteer is a play about voices that have not yet found the words to speak — but who want the world to know the Aberfan disaster was not “an act of God”, and that future disasters in former mining areas can and must be prevented. 

Avant Cymru presents The Silent Volunteer, a play by Sue Bevan, alongside an exhibition and Q&A in partnership with Coalfield Regeneration. 

To mark the 60th anniversary of the Aberfan Disaster, the descendants of the volunteers are opening up a conversation about how this history continues to shape mining communities today — and why remembering, listening and learning still matters.

show.description:

Bryn Cartwright (William Thomas) a wealthy roofing contractor, rugby club chairman and local kingpin rules the roost until Fatty Lewis (Huw Ceredig) a local handyman falls off a ladder on a Cartwright job. Fatty’s twin junkie grandsons, Julian (Llyr Ifans) and Jeremy (Rhys Ifans) who are not in fact twins –attempt to procure compensation from Cartwright, who refuses to pay up. The doped-up Julian and Jeremy then inflict anarchy not only on Cartwright and his family but on anyone they encounter whilst Terry (Dougray Scott) and Greyo (Dorian Thomas), two local policemen employ their own dubious peacekeeping methods as events spiral out of control.

22 reasons why Twin Town is the greatest Welsh cult film of all time

show.name: Very Santana
show.description:
THE ULTIMATE CARLOS SANTANA EXPERIENCE 

 Step into the world of Carlos Santana and experience the music, the sound and the spirit of one of the greatest guitar legends of all time. 
Very Santana takes you on a musical journey spanning the entire Carlos Santana legacy  from the ground breaking Abraxas era and timeless classics such as Black Magic Woman, Oye Como Va and Samba Pa Ti, through the late-70s favourites Europa and She's Not There, all the way to the multi-Grammy-winning modern era with Smooth, Maria Maria and more.
But this is far more than a collection of Santana songs.  Our exceptional musicians recreate the energy, musicianship and spontaneity of a Santana live concert, bringing these iconic songs to life with extended arrangements, powerful grooves and plenty of improvisation.
No two shows are ever quite the same keeping the music fresh, exciting and full of surprises, even for those who return year after year.  And they do return. Hundreds of independent reviews have praised Very Santana for its authenticity, musicianship and sheer enjoyment of performing this extraordinary music. 
At the heart of the performance is the unmistakable Santana sound: warm, all-analogue, valve-driven guitar tones, created using PRS, Gibson and Fibenare guitars alongside Mesa Boogie amplifiers. Add Hammond organ & Fender Rhodes sounds, drums, bass and an abundance of percussion, and you have the ingredients for a truly immersive Santana experience.  Then there's Amera, whose powerful vocals, stage presence and dance moves bring an extra dimension to the performance. 
Very Santana is not simply a tribute band. It's a celebration of the music, the sound and the spirit of Carlos Santana performed live, with passion, authenticity and plenty of soul. 
Come and experience the magic for yourself. 
 Don't miss the show. Get your tickets and join us for the Santana Experience!

show.name: Ward Thomas
show.description:
Country-pop duo Ward Thomas have announced a series of intimate and stripped-back live shows for Spring 2027. 

The announcement comes whilst Ward Thomas are currently on tour celebrating the 10th anniversary of their landmark No.1 album, Cartwheels, which was the first ever record by a UK country act to top the charts. Sisters Catherine and Lizzy also performed earlier this month at the Last Night of the Proms tribute to Dolly Parton, 
Now for 2027 they will tour intimate venues across the UK performing a special acoustic set with stripped back versions of songs from across their back catalogue, putting their renowned harmonies, musicianship and songwriting front and centre. The duo will also share the stories and inspiration behind the music that has seen them make such a lasting impact on the UK Country music scene. 
Recording their debut album, 2014’s ‘From Where We Stand’, whilst still in school, the duo have since cemented themselves as pioneers in the UK Country and Americana scene; not least for the follow-up album ‘Cartwheels’ released in 2016 going to No.1 in the UK Album Charts, the first by a UK country act to top the charts. 
In 2019, the band were presented with the Country Music Association’s Jeff Walker Global Achievement Award in recognition of their success and impact on country music in the UK. 
Their fifth studio album, Music In The Madness, released in 2023, showcased the duo’s trademark harmony-led sound while continuing their evolution as artists.

They will be joined by very special guest Katherine Priddy
